newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady-weak, with declines expected from an increase in hog marketings and projections for less demand next week, livestock dealers said.

Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs at the plant could range $51.50 to $52.00 per cwt and Illinois hogs at the plant could range $50.00 to $50.50. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could span $51.00 to $51.50.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog marketings Wednesday were 108,000 head, above the estimate of 100,000, USDA said. Thursday's marketings were estimated at 105,000 head.
The 105,000 head estimate was above 97,000 marketed a week ago, USDA said.

Weakness in the direct hog market also could be generated by the reduction of operations at IBP's plant in Columbus Junction, Iowa. IBP this week announced it would cease second shift slaughter at the plant indefinitely starting Monday.
The plant has an estimated daily slaughter capacity of 13,000 head, according to industry sources.
Prices could be underpinned by firm pork prices. Fresh hams at middday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher and pork bellies were $2.00 higher, USDA said.
